It has been studied more closely than any other spring on the plateau.

items.stem: Based on the text, what does Okafor indicate about Hale's 1874 version of the ballad?

It was probably copied by Hale himself from the 1852 Bristol broadside.
It shows that most songs Hale collected in Dorset came from printed sheets.
It differs enough from the 1852 broadside to show decades of oral change.

items.subtype_name: Which choice best describes X / what does the text indicate about X
items.stimulus: When the city of Marlow narrowed Fenn Avenue from four lanes to two in 2019, planners expected its traffic to shift onto parallel Corder Street. Counts a year later showed that Fenn carried about a third fewer cars, while Corder carried only slightly more than before. Surveys found that some former Fenn drivers now used the ring road and that others had switched to a bus line added the same year. The planners concluded that much of Fenn's lost traffic had not moved to Corder at all but had gone farther afield or out of cars entirely.
items.stem: Based on the text, what did the planners conclude about the traffic that Fenn Avenue lost?
choices: Most of it shifted onto Corder Street, as the planners had predicted.
Much of it vanished because the narrowing led people to make fewer trips.
Most of it moved to the bus line, which was added to absorb Fenn's traffic.
Much of it went to a more distant road or to transit instead of to Corder.
items.explanation: The last sentence puts the facts together. Much of the lost traffic did not go to Corder. It went 'farther afield', which the surveys identify as the ring road, or 'out of cars', meaning onto the bus line. This choice combines both destinations and keeps the planners' word 'much'.

C.why: You noticed the bus line and made it the whole answer. The text says 'some' drivers switched to it, not most, and never says why the bus line was added.
